**{fmt}** is an open-source formatting library providing a fast and safe
alternative to C stdio and C++ iostreams.

If you like this project, please consider donating to one of the funds that
help victims of the war in Ukraine: https://www.stopputin.net/.

`Documentation <https://fmt.dev>`__

`Cheat Sheets <https://hackingcpp.com/cpp/libs/fmt.html>`__

Q&A: ask questions on `StackOverflow with the tag fmt
<https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/fmt>`_.

Try {fmt} in `Compiler Explorer <https://godbolt.org/z/Eq5763>`_.

Features
--------

* Simple `format API <https://fmt.dev/latest/api.html>`_ with positional arguments
  for localization
* Implementation of `C++20 std::format
  <https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/format>`__
* `Format string syntax <https://fmt.dev/latest/syntax.html>`_ similar to Python's
  `format <https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.format>`_
* Fast IEEE 754 floating-point formatter with correct rounding, shortness and
  round-trip guarantees

part.text:
Implemented the fix in `include/fmt/ranges.h` and `include/fmt/core.h`.

Key changes:
- Propagate debug formatting through nested range formatters so `vector<vector<char>>` and split ranges print quoted chars.
- Bind range elements to an lvalue before mapping, fixing the ambiguous/failed `write` calls for ranges whose `begin()`/`end()` are non-const.
- Use `const T&` in string-view convertibility checks, avoiding false positives from C++23’s range constructor for `std::string_view`.

Validation:
- `ranges-test`: 25/25 passed.
- Full `ctest`: 20/20 passed.
- Both issue examples and the nested `split`/`transform` case compile and produce the expected output under C++20 and C++23.
